From fe11e5c40817b84abaa5d83bfb6586d8412bfd07 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kai Ma <k4729.23098@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 22:54:18 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: reject zero shift in nft_bitwise

Reject zero shift operands for nft_bitwise left and right shift
expressions during initialization.

The carry propagation logic computes the carry from the adjacent 32-bit
word using BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift. A zero shift operand turns this
into a 32-bit shift, which is undefined behaviour.

Reject zero shift operands in the control plane, alongside the existing
check for values greater than or equal to 32, so malformed rules never
reach the packet path.

Fixes: 567d746b55bc ("netfilter: bitwise: add support for shifts.")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
Reported-by: Yuan Tan <yuantan098@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Kai Ma <k4729.23098@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Ren Wei <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_bitwise.c b/net/netfilter/nft_bitwise.c
index 13808e9cd999..94dccdcfa06b 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_bitwise.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_bitwise.c
@@ -196,7 +196,8 @@ static int nft_bitwise_init_shift(struct nft_bitwise *priv,
 	if (err < 0)
 		return err;
 
-	if (priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)) {
+	if (!priv->data.data[0] ||
+	    priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)) {
 		nft_data_release(&priv->data, desc.type);
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file to fix a bug in the netfilter bitwise expression handler.

### Modifications in each file:
- **`net/netfilter/nft_bitwise.c`**: In the `nft_bitwise_init_shift` function, the condition that validates the shift amount is extended. Originally it only rejected shift values greater than or equal to `BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)` (i.e., ≥ 32). The patch adds an additional check that rejects a shift value of zero (`!priv->data.data[0]`). Both conditions are combined with a logical OR, so the function now returns `-EINVAL` if the shift operand is zero or out of range.

### Relationships between the modifications:
The modification is a single, focused change in one function. The relationship is straightforward: the new check complements the existing bounds check to prevent a specific class of undefined behavior. The zero shift case was previously uncaught, leading to undefined behavior in the packet path when the shift amount was used in carry propagation logic (which computed `BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift`, producing a 32‑bit shift when `shift == 0`). By rejecting zero shifts at rule initialization time (control plane), malformed rules are prevented from ever reaching the data path.

Fixes: 567d746b55bc ("netfilter: bitwise: add support for shifts.")

Here is the root cause:
The nft_bitwise_init_shift function did not reject zero shift operands. When a shift of 0 is used, the carry propagation logic computes BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift, resulting in a 32-bit shift of a 32-bit value, which is undefined behavior in C, causing incorrect computation or potential crashes.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int nft_bitwise_init_shift(struct nft_bitwise *priv,
 				  const struct nlattr *const tb[])
 {
 	struct nft_data_desc desc = {
 		.type	= NFT_DATA_VALUE,
 		.size	= sizeof(priv->data),
 		.len	= sizeof(u32),
 	};
 	int err;
 
 	if (tb[NFTA_BITWISE_MASK] ||
 	    tb[NFTA_BITWISE_XOR]  ||
 	    tb[NFTA_BITWISE_SREG2])
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	if (!tb[NFTA_BITWISE_DATA])
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	err = nft_data_init(NULL, &priv->data, &desc, tb[NFTA_BITWISE_DATA]);
 	if (err < 0)
 		return err;
 
-	if (priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)) {
+	if (!priv->data.data[0] ||
+	    priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32)) {
 		nft_data_release(&priv->data, desc.type);
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
